#### `event_bin_value`

```c
int32_t as_udf_event_bin_value(int32_t which, const char* name, int32_t name_len, void* out, int32_t cap)
```

Read a bin of one of an event's records into `out` as a 16-byte value (`cap` at least 16): `which` is 0 for the
current record, 1 for the incoming one, and `name` is `name_len` bytes. Returns AS_UDF_OK; AS_UDF_NOT_FOUND
when that record has no such bin, when there is no such record (the call is not an event, or the side is
absent) or the name is not a bin name; AS_UDF_ERR when `cap` is under 16. Unlike as_udf_rec_bin_value, `out` is
left as it was on AS_UDF_NOT_FOUND. as_udf_event_bin is this call on a decoded record.

#### `as_udf_event_record`

```c
typedef struct as_udf_event_record_s {
	int32_t which;            /* 0 current, 1 incoming */
	int64_t generation;
	int64_t last_update_time;
	int64_t source_id;
	as_udf_value bin_names;   /* list of bin names */
	as_udf_value deleted_bins; /* list of bin names this side deleted; AS_UDF_ABSENT, not an empty list, when none */
	as_udf_value bin_last_update_times; /* map name -> last-update time, per bin (AS_UDF_ABSENT if the server sent none) */
	as_udf_value bin_source_ids; /* map name -> source id, likewise */
	bool is_delete;           /* incoming: the write is a record delete, so this record has no bins */
	bool is_partial;          /* incoming: the write carries only the bins that changed */
	bool is_tombstone;        /* current: the record exists but has no bins */
} as_udf_event_record;
```

One of the two records of an xdr-merge, as as_udf_event_decode fills it: its metadata, its bin names, and the
facts of the merge that are about this record. Read-only: its bins are read with the `as_udf_event_` functions
and nothing writes it; the handler's answer is what changes the record. `source_id` is the XDR source id of the
cluster that wrote this version. `generation` and `last_update_time` are 0 on both records
of an xdr-merge: each cluster has its own, so a merge that read them could not converge, and it is the per-bin
times that order the two sides. A metadata field the server did not send is 0. The list and map fields are
values to read by position, of kind AS_UDF_ABSENT when the server sent none; read the per-bin maps through
as_udf_event_bin_last_update_time and as_udf_event_bin_source_id, which fall back to the record's. A fact that
is about the other record is false here.

`deleted_bins` has one of two shapes, and never a third: a list of names (kind AS_UDF_LIST)
when there are some, and no value at all (kind AS_UDF_ABSENT) when there are none. The server does not send an
empty list for "none". So do not read `.len` without testing the kind: as_udf_list_count answers the count for
either shape, as_udf_list_has_string answers false for the absent one, and as_udf_event_deleted_any is the
test for `deleted_bins`.

#### `as_udf_map_get`

```c
as_udf_value as_udf_map_get(const as_udf_value* m, const char* key)
```

The entry under a NUL-terminated string key of a stored map, as a value. Of kind AS_UDF_ABSENT when there is no
such key or `m` is not of kind AS_UDF_MAP: a key the map does not have is nothing, not an error. An entry that
holds nil is of kind AS_UDF_NIL. The lookup is linear in the map's entries. For a map bin, a nested map, or a
map argument; a map being built is asked with as_udf_map_contains.

The entry under an integer key of a stored map, as a value. Of kind AS_UDF_ABSENT when there is no such key or

The integer under a NUL-terminated string key of a stored map, into `out`. Returns AS_UDF_OK; AS_UDF_NOT_FOUND,

The integer under a NUL-terminated string key of a stored map into `out`, or `dflt` when there is nothing

#### `as_udf_string_eq`

```c
bool as_udf_string_eq(const as_udf_value* v, const char* text, int32_t n, char* buf)
```

Whether a stored string value is exactly the `n` bytes at `text`, read through `buf`, which holds at least `n`
bytes. Plumbing of as_udf_string_is and as_udf_list_has_string, which size the buffer.

#### `as_udf_string_is`

```c
bool as_udf_string_is(const as_udf_value* v, const char* text)
```

Whether a stored string value reads as the NUL-terminated `text`, of any length. False when `v` is not of kind
AS_UDF_STR: GeoJSON text is not a string. The lengths are compared first, and only a string as long as `text`
is copied out, into as many bytes of stack as `text` is long; so a `text` of many kilobytes needs a stack that
size (clang's default for wasm32 is 64 KB; `-Wl,-z,stack-size=N` raises it).

#### `as_udf_event_side`

```c
bool as_udf_event_side(const as_udf_value* description, const char* key, int32_t which, as_udf_event_record* out)
```

Decode the record under `key` ("current" or "incoming") of the event's description map into `out`, marked as
record `which` for as_udf_event_bin, with the facts that are about that record. False when the entry is not a
map or carries no list of bins; `out` is then partly filled and not to be used. Plumbing of
as_udf_event_decode, which is what a handler calls.

#### `as_udf_event_decode`

```c
int32_t as_udf_event_decode(int32_t args, int32_t argc, as_udf_event_record* current, as_udf_event_record* incoming)
```

Decode an xdr-merge call's arguments into its two records: `current`, the record as it is on this cluster, and
`incoming`, the one that arrived over XDR. `args` and `argc` are the handler's own parameters. Returns
AS_UDF_OK, or AS_UDF_ERR when the arguments are not those of an xdr-merge, in which case neither record is to
be used and the handler should fail. Call it once, first: the records hold values that stay valid for the whole
call.

#### `as_udf_event_bin`

```c
int32_t as_udf_event_bin(const as_udf_event_record* r, const char* name, as_udf_value* out)
```

Read a bin of one of the event's records, of any kind, into `out`; `name` is NUL-terminated. Returns AS_UDF_OK,
or AS_UDF_NOT_FOUND when that record has no such bin, which leaves `out` as it was. A bin the incoming write
does not carry is not found even if the other cluster has it (see `is_partial`), and so is a bin that side
deleted (see `deleted_bins`).

Whether one of the event's records has the bin. False for a bin that side deleted or that a partial incoming

A bin of one of the event's records as an integer, into `out`. Returns AS_UDF_OK with the value;

int64_t mine, theirs;

#### `as_udf_list_count`

```c
int32_t as_udf_list_count(const as_udf_value* list)
```

How many elements a list value has, and 0 for a value that is not a list. The count for the fields of an event
record that are a list or nothing at all: `deleted_bins` is of kind AS_UDF_LIST when the server sent the
names and of kind AS_UDF_ABSENT when it sent none, and never an empty list for "none". This answers the
count either way, so a handler need not test the kind first: `as_udf_list_count(&incoming.deleted_bins)`.

#### `as_udf_event_deleted_any`

```c
bool as_udf_event_deleted_any(const as_udf_event_record* r)
```

Whether this side deleted any bin: its `deleted_bins` list is there and not empty (the field is a list of
names, or of kind AS_UDF_ABSENT when this side deleted none; as_udf_list_count answers its length either
way). The case every merge has to guard against, since a deleted bin reads as absent and taking the other
side's copy would bring it back; as_udf_list_has_string on `deleted_bins` says whether a given bin was one of
them.

#### `as_udf_event_bin_last_update_time`

```c
int64_t as_udf_event_bin_last_update_time(const as_udf_event_record* r, const char* name)
```

When this side last wrote the bin, as the server's timestamp for it, in milliseconds since the Citrusleaf
epoch, 2010-01-01T00:00:00Z (Unix milliseconds minus 1262304000000). The server gives a time for every bin of
both sides, a bin the side deleted included: for a write that came from another cluster, the time that cluster
shipped, or, where it shipped none, the time the write arrived here. A bin with no time of its own, one the
record neither has nor deleted, gets the record's `last_update_time`, which in an xdr-merge is 0. `name` is
NUL-terminated. A number to order the two sides by, not to compare with a clock, which a handler does not
have.

#### `as_udf_event_bin_source_id`

```c
int64_t as_udf_event_bin_source_id(const as_udf_event_record* r, const char* name)
```

The id of the XDR source that last wrote the bin on this side. The server gives one for every bin of both
sides; a bin with none of its own gets the record's source id. What breaks a tie between equal last-update
times.

#### `as_udf_event_incoming_is_newer`

```c
bool as_udf_event_incoming_is_newer(const as_udf_event_record* current, const as_udf_event_record* incoming, const char* name)
```

Whether the incoming record wrote the bin later than the current one: by last-update time, then by source id.
Both clusters see the same two times and ids, so both give the same side as newer whichever of them is
`current`: a rule built on this is symmetric. False when the two are equal in both.

#### `as_udf_list_has_string`

```c
bool as_udf_list_has_string(const as_udf_value* list, const char* text)
```

Whether a stored list holds the string `text` (NUL-terminated, of any length) among its elements; elements
that are not strings are not it. False when `list` is not of kind AS_UDF_LIST, which includes the
AS_UDF_ABSENT of an event record's `deleted_bins` when there are none. Linear in the list. Only
elements as long as `text` are copied out, into as many bytes of stack as `text` is long (see
as_udf_string_is). The walk takes one handle for its cursor and gives it back before it returns; when the
call's memory has no room for one it cannot be made, and the answer is found the slow way, an element at a time, rather than given as false. For an
event record's `bin_names` and `deleted_bins`, and any list of strings.

#### `as_udf_event_with_bins`

```c
int32_t as_udf_event_with_bins(const as_udf_event_record* r, int32_t overrides)
```

Put every bin of one of the event's records that the built map `overrides` lacks into it, by position, and
return the map's handle: that record with `overrides` on top. For a handler that decides a few bins and keeps
the rest of one record. A bin this side deleted is not among its bins, so it is not put and the answer leaves
it out: nothing is brought back. Returns `overrides`, or 0 when a bin could not be carried over (its name or
value could not be read, or the map did not take it): 0 is no handle, and as_udf_resolve_record fails the call
for it, so a record answer is never built short of a bin. It prefers a side, so two clusters that each use it
on their own current record do not converge; use it on a side both agree on, such as the one
as_udf_event_incoming_is_newer names.
```c
int32_t out = as_udf_map_new(8);
as_udf_map_put_string_int(out, "visits", 6, visits);
return as_udf_resolve_record(as_udf_event_with_bins(&incoming, out));
```

#### `as_udf_map_find`

```c
int32_t as_udf_map_find(const as_udf_value* m, const as_udf_value* key, as_udf_value* out)
```

The value under `key`, a key read from another map, in the stored map `m`, into `out`: a string key is matched
by its bytes, an integer key by its value, and never one by the other. Returns AS_UDF_OK; AS_UDF_NOT_FOUND, with
`out` of kind AS_UDF_ABSENT, when there is no such key or `m` is not a map; AS_UDF_TYPE_MISMATCH for a key that
is neither a string nor an integer; AS_UDF_REFUSED when the call's memory has no room for the walk a long key
needs. A string key of up to 256 bytes is looked up in one host call; a longer one is compared with each key
of `m` (as_udf_cmp_stored), which needs no buffer. An entry that holds nil is found, with kind AS_UDF_NIL.

#### `as_udf_max_per_key`

```c
int32_t as_udf_max_per_key(const as_udf_value* current, const as_udf_value* incoming, int32_t* map)
```

The per-key maximum of two maps: a new map with every key of either side, each under the larger of its two
values, or under its one value when only one side has the key. Built on the host, so it is ordered by key and
both clusters build the same bytes. A side is missing when it is NULL, absent or nil; otherwise it must be a map
whose keys are strings or integers and whose values are integers. Returns AS_UDF_OK with the map's handle in
`*map` (close it once it is stored or put); AS_UDF_NOT_FOUND when both sides are missing; AS_UDF_TYPE_MISMATCH
for anything else, a side that is not a map included, since a merge does not guess what a double or a nested map
should become; AS_UDF_REFUSED when the host does not build the map. Nothing is left open on a failure.

Symmetric (the two sides swapped give the same map), idempotent (merging a map with itself, or with a merge it is
part of, changes nothing) and associative (three sides merge to the same map in any order): the laws a
convergent merge needs. It is the merge of any map of values that only grow; as_udf_counter_merge is the same
merge under the name of the structure it serves.
```c
as_udf_value mine, theirs;
int32_t merged;
if (as_udf_event_map(&current, "seen", &mine) == AS_UDF_TYPE_MISMATCH ||
		as_udf_event_map(&incoming, "seen", &theirs) == AS_UDF_TYPE_MISMATCH) return as_udf_fail_str("seen is not a map");
int32_t rc = as_udf_max_per_key(&mine, &theirs, &merged);
if (rc == AS_UDF_OK) as_udf_map_put_string_handle(out, "seen", 4, merged);
else if (rc != AS_UDF_NOT_FOUND) return as_udf_fail_str("seen is not a map of integers");
```

#### `as_udf_sorted_union`

```c
int32_t as_udf_sorted_union(const as_udf_value* current, const as_udf_value* incoming, int32_t* list)
```

The union of two lists as a set: a new list with every element of either side once, sorted, so both clusters
build the same bytes whatever order the elements arrived in. The elements are integers, strings or blobs: the
kinds the server keys a map by, since the host sorts them as a map built on it sorts its keys. Integers come
first, by value, then strings and then blobs, each by its bytes; an integer and a string are never the same
element, however they read. A side is missing when it is NULL, absent or nil; otherwise it must be a list of
those kinds. Returns AS_UDF_OK with the list's handle in `*list`; AS_UDF_NOT_FOUND when both sides are missing;
AS_UDF_TYPE_MISMATCH for a side that is not a list or an element of another kind (a double, a nested list or
map, nil); AS_UDF_REFUSED when the host does not build the list.

Symmetric, idempotent and associative: the merge of a set that only grows. A removal needs a second set, as the
2P-Set of the CRDT tutorial keeps one.
```c
int32_t tags;
if (as_udf_sorted_union(&mine, &theirs, &tags) == AS_UDF_OK) as_udf_map_put_string_handle(out, "tags", 4, tags);
```

#### `as_udf_counter_merge`

```c
int32_t as_udf_counter_merge(const as_udf_value* current, const as_udf_value* incoming, int32_t* map)
```

The merge of a per-origin counter: a map of origin to count, each origin's count raised only by the cluster it
names, merged by the larger count per origin. It is as_udf_max_per_key under the name of the structure: the same
rules, the same statuses, and AS_UDF_NOT_FOUND when both sides are missing. as_udf_counter_total reads the
counter's value. Symmetric, idempotent and associative. A count that goes down is not a count this merges: a
PN-Counter keeps a second counter for the decrements.
```c
int32_t hits;
if (as_udf_counter_merge(&mine, &theirs, &hits) == AS_UDF_OK) as_udf_map_put_string_handle(out, "hits", 4, hits);
```

#### `as_udf_counter_total`

```c
int32_t as_udf_counter_total(const as_udf_value* counter, int64_t* total)
```

The value of a per-origin counter: the sum of its counts, wrapping on overflow, into `total`. A missing counter
(NULL, absent or nil) counts 0. Returns AS_UDF_OK; AS_UDF_TYPE_MISMATCH, with `total` untouched, when it is not a
map, or when a key is not a string or an integer or a count is not an integer, as for as_udf_counter_merge;
AS_UDF_REFUSED when the call's memory has no room for the walk.
```c
as_udf_value hits;
int64_t total;
if (as_udf_rec_map("hits", &hits) == AS_UDF_TYPE_MISMATCH || as_udf_counter_total(&hits, &total) != AS_UDF_OK) {
	return as_udf_fail_str("hits is not a counter");
}
```

#### `as_udf_lww_by_version`

```c
int32_t as_udf_lww_by_version(const as_udf_value* current, const as_udf_value* incoming, as_udf_value* winner)
```

Last writer wins by an application version: of two `[version, value]` lists, the one with the higher version,
as it is, to write back, into `winner`. Two equal versions are decided by the lists' stored bytes, the greater
winning, so both clusters pick the same side; two lists with the same bytes are the same either way. A side is
missing when it is NULL, absent or nil; otherwise it must be a list of exactly two elements whose first is an
integer. The value may be of any kind. Returns AS_UDF_OK; AS_UDF_NOT_FOUND when both sides are missing;
AS_UDF_TYPE_MISMATCH for a side of any other shape.

Symmetric, idempotent and associative: it is the larger of the two by version, then by bytes, which is a total
order. The version is the application's, raised by every write that changes the value, so no clock decides.
The write UDF moves the version and the value in one write.
```c
as_udf_value price;
if (as_udf_lww_by_version(&mine, &theirs, &price) == AS_UDF_OK) as_udf_map_put_value(out, "price", &price);
```

#### `as_udf_resolve_keep_local`

```c
int32_t as_udf_resolve_keep_local(void) { as_udf_result_string("keep-local", 10); return 0; }
```

Answer `keep-local`: the record on this cluster stays as it is and the incoming write is dropped. Sets the
call's result and returns 0, the status the handler returns: `return as_udf_resolve_keep_local();`.

#### `as_udf_resolve_take_remote`

```c
int32_t as_udf_resolve_take_remote(void) { as_udf_result_string("take-remote", 11); return 0; }
```

Answer `take-remote`: the incoming write is applied, its bins over the current record. Sets the call's result
and returns 0, the status the handler returns: `return as_udf_resolve_take_remote();`.

#### `as_udf_resolve_policy`

```c
int32_t as_udf_resolve_policy(void) { as_udf_result_string("policy", 6); return 0; }
```

Answer `policy`: what the server would have done without a handler. A set bound to a handler never uses bin
convergence, so this applies the incoming write, as `take-remote` does. The answer for the cases a handler has
no opinion on. Sets the call's result and returns 0, the status the handler returns:
`return as_udf_resolve_policy();`.

#### `as_udf_resolve_delete`

```c
int32_t as_udf_resolve_delete(void) { as_udf_result_string("delete", 6); return 0; }
```

Answer `delete`: the record is removed on this cluster and a durable tombstone is left, so a late write cannot
bring it back. The delete is not shipped: the other cluster decides for itself, so a merge that deletes has to
delete on both sides for the two to agree. A record answer with no bins left in it is not this: it is the
handler's failure. Sets the call's result and returns 0, the status the handler returns: `return
as_udf_resolve_delete();`.

#### `as_udf_resolve_expunge`

```c
int32_t as_udf_resolve_expunge(void) { as_udf_result_string("expunge", 7); return 0; }
```

Answer `expunge`: the record is removed on this cluster outright, with no tombstone, so a later write creates
it again. Like `delete`, it is not shipped to the other cluster. Sets the call's result and returns 0, the
status the handler returns: `return as_udf_resolve_expunge();`.

#### `as_udf_resolve_record`

```c
int32_t as_udf_resolve_record(int32_t bins)
```

Answer with the final record. `bins` is the handle of a built map from bin name to value: the record is left
with exactly these bins, a bin that is absent from the map or nil in it is deleted, and at least one bin must
remain. No answer carries a TTL: the server gives the merged record the later of the two records' expirations,
and a record that never expires wins. Returns the status the handler returns: 0, or non-zero with the call
failed when the answer could not be built.
```c
int32_t out = as_udf_map_new(4);
int64_t a, b;
if (as_udf_event_int_or(&current, "visits", 0, &a) != AS_UDF_OK) return as_udf_fail_str("visits is not an integer");
if (as_udf_event_int_or(&incoming, "visits", 0, &b) != AS_UDF_OK) return as_udf_fail_str("visits is not an integer");
as_udf_map_put_string_int(out, "visits", 6, a > b ? a : b);
return as_udf_resolve_record(out);
```

#### `AS_UDF_EVENT_XDR_MERGE(name)`

```c
#define AS_UDF_EVENT_XDR_MERGE(name)                                                                       \
	AS_UDF_SIGNATURE(name, "event xdr-merge/1 " #name "(current: record, incoming: record) -> resolution") \
	AS_UDF_EXPORT(name) int32_t name(int32_t args, int32_t argc)
```

Declare an xdr-merge handler: `AS_UDF_EVENT_XDR_MERGE(name) { ... }` defines and exports `int32_t name(int32_t
args, int32_t argc)` and the signature `event-set` checks before binding it. The body decodes the two records
with as_udf_event_decode and returns one of the `as_udf_resolve_` answers. A handler cannot write a record,
read the clock or log, and must be symmetric: both clusters resolve the same pair with the sides swapped and
have to land on the same record.
```c
AS_UDF_EVENT_XDR_MERGE(newest_wins)
{
	as_udf_event_record current, incoming;
	if (as_udf_event_decode(args, argc, &current, &incoming) != AS_UDF_OK) return as_udf_fail_str("not an xdr-merge");
	if (incoming.is_delete) return as_udf_resolve_policy();
	return as_udf_event_incoming_is_newer(&current, &incoming, "profile") ?
		as_udf_resolve_take_remote() : as_udf_resolve_keep_local();
}
```
